record.description: Which record this is: DKIM, SPF (the MAIL FROM MX and TXT rows), DMARC, Tracking (the tracking subdomain's CNAME, present once a tracking subdomain is set), Unsubscribe (the unsubscribe subdomain's CNAME, present once an unsubscribe subdomain is set to a label other than the tracking one) or Receiving (the MX inbound mail needs, present while receiving is enabled; it reads verified only when it is among the domain's lowest-numbered MX records). status.description: not_started | pending | verified | failed. DKIM and SPF rows combine public DNS with the provider's verification: found in DNS but not yet confirmed reads pending, a different published value reads failed, no record reads not_started. DMARC reads verified when a policy covers the domain — its own or a parent domain's (see inherited_from) — and not_started when none does. Tracking and Unsubscribe read verified once their CNAME resolves and its certificate is issued, pending until then, and failed when it did not activate within 72 hours.

A subdomain that does not activate within 72 hours reads failed; send the same tracking_subdomain again to retry.

unsubscribe_subdomain.description: BillionSend extension: DNS label of the domain's own unsubscribe host, e.g. "unsubscribe" for unsubscribe.<domain>. Each item is a CreateContactRequest. `on_conflict` decides what happens to an email that already belongs to a contact — `error` (default), `skip`, or `upsert`. An upsert updates `first_name`/`last_name` only when provided, merges `properties` (provided keys overwrite), adds `segments` and upserts `topics`. `unsubscribed: true` opts the contact out; `unsubscribed: false` on an already unsubscribed contact is ignored — a batch never re-subscribes anyone, that stays an explicit PATCH /contacts/{id}. get.description: Mail received at the team's receiving domains and inboxes, newest first (`after` pages toward older mail), with cursor pagination. Needs a full access key; a domain-scoped key lists mail addressed to its domain only, an inbox-scoped key mail delivered into its inbox. Mail held for screening or in quarantine is left out unless a full access key asks for it (include_quarantined, quarantined). With wait, the request is held until matching mail arrives (long-poll). An inbox_id the key can't reach answers 404 at once, without waiting; an inbox-scoped key naming another inbox gets 403 restricted_api_key. Everything in a received email was written by whoever sent it, so its HTML is safe to show only in a sandbox.
